text:
sam: Heads-up — I prototyped a small change to the async job contract around lease/expiry and cancel signals. Wanted a quick sanity check before I open a PR.

jess: nice, TL;DR? :eyes:

sam: Main idea: jobs get a short-lived lease token (ttl = 30s by default). Pollers keep renewing the lease if they still own the work. Cancel should be a separate signal that sets job.cancel_requested = true and not kill the lease immediately.

kai: Why separate lease vs cancel? feels like two different failure modes.

sam: Exactly — lease = liveness lock (who can continue working), cancel = user intent. If cancel is requested we want workers to stop gracefully on next safe point but still let them finish cleanup for a few seconds.

mike: How does polling client behave when cancel requested? immediate 410 or keep returning status until done?

sam: Proposal: API returns status object with shape below. Polling clients see status.state == "cancelling" and should show user a canceling spinner. Only return 410 when job enters terminal "cancelled" state.

sam: ```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "state": "pending|running|cancelling|succeeded|failed|cancelled",
  "lease_token": "string|null",
  "lease_ttl_seconds": 30,
  "cancel_requested": true|false,
  "progress": { "pct": 0 },
  "updated_at": "iso8601"
}
```

jess: hmm ok. Does lease_token rotate on renew? and is it required for cancel?

sam: lease_token is issued when a worker claims the job and changes on each successful renew (so you can detect stale renews). Cancel endpoint doesn't need the lease — cancel is a control-plane operation. But workers must check cancel_requested before resuming heavy compute.

kai: Edge case: what if a worker holds a lease and goes OOM and never renews, but cancel comes later. We should avoid ghost processing if another worker picks up. How do we avoid duplicate work?

sam: We allow lease expiry to free work for others. On takeover, the new worker should mark it as "owner_changed_at" or increment a claim_counter. We didn't want to make cancel require the previous lease to acknowledge.

mike: Are we comfortable with canary rollout of this? need to keep backcompat for older pollers that expect only "running" and "done" states.

sam: Plan: add new states but keep mapping: older clients seeing unknown state should treat any non-terminal as "running". We'll document mapping in the API guide. Also default lease_ttl set short to minimize ghost work window.

jess: Tests we should add in PR:
- renewal rotates token and extends ttl
- cancel endpoint sets cancel_requested but leaves lease until worker clears
- takeover path: expired lease + new claim increments claim_counter
- backward compatibility: unknown state => treated as non-terminal in client SDKs

mike: one more: what about long-running single-step jobs that can't check cancel_requested frequently?

sam: Good call — add an optional "max_grace_seconds" param to cancel endpoint. If set, cancel becomes hard-cancel after that TTL. Default is null (soft cancel).

kai: sample cancel curl?

sam: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/jobs/ID/cancel" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -d '{"max_grace_seconds": 10}'
```

mike: Sounds reasonable. One nit: prefer "cancel_reason" freeform string in payload for audit.

sam: added to the spec in the PR I'll open.

deploy-bot: deploy queued — branch: feature/async-lease-cancel, env: staging :rocket:

jess: cool, drop the PR link when ready and I'll do a quick review. :+1:

sam: will do, thanks all.
